As artificial intelligence becomes more integrated into daily life, debates  around  its  ethical  use  are  growing  louder.  Machines now make decisions that  were  once  the  (91)  ______  of human judgment-from recommending medical treatments to scanning resumes. While AI offers speed and efficiency, it lacks moral (92) ______, raising concerns about bias, accountability, and transparency. Critics argue that without strict ethical frameworks, AI could reinforce social inequalities or even make harmful  choices  with  no  clear  line  of  (93)  ______.  Developers face  the  challenge  of  embedding  values  into  code-yet  whose values  should  apply? In multicultural societies, defining what is "right" is rarely (94) ______. Some suggest collaborative oversight involving ethicists, technologists, and policymakers. Others warn that  regulation  must  evolve  faster  than  innovation  to  prevent misuse.  In  the  race to build smarter systems, the real question remains: can we create machines that are not just intelligent, but also (95) ______ ?
SSC Stenographer 07/08/2025 (Shift 1)

In modern societies, the concept of freedom is often celebrated as an essential right. However, true freedom is not the absence of  rules  but  the  presence  of  thoughtful  (96)  _____.  Without  it, freedom risks turning  into  chaos,  where  individual  actions undermine collective welfare. A society that prizes only personal liberty  without  shared  responsibility  may  soon  face  moral  and civic  (97)______.  While  people often equate freedom with doing as  they  please,  meaningful  liberty  requires  a  commitment  to boundaries  that  preserve  dignity  and  (98)  _____  for  all.  This balance is difficult to maintain, especially in democracies where voices are many  and  interests  often  (99)______.  Yet,  it  is precisely  through  dialogue,  compromise,  and  mutual  respect that  freedom  finds  its  most  enduring  expression.  In  the  end, freedom  divorced  from  responsibility  is  not  progress,  but  a subtle (100) ______ of what it truly means to be free.
SSC Stenographer 07/08/2025 (Shift 2)

items.text: As  technology  continues  to  advance,  space  exploration  is  no longer  limited  to  astronauts  and  scientists.  In  the  coming decades, space could become a place for engineers, architects, doctors,  and  even  artists.  The  idea  of  working  beyond  Earth, once  considered  science  fiction,  is  slowly  becoming a realistic (101)_______ . Many countries  have  already  started  investing  in training programs that prepare students for space-related fields. These  programs  not  only  focus  on  science,  but  also  build problem-solving  and  leadership  skills.  Working  in  space  will bring its own challenges-long durations, isolation, and technical failures  will require (102)_______ preparation. Yet, the chance to be  part  of  something  bigger  than  oneself  is  what draws many young  minds. With space tourism rising and private companies joining  the  race,  the  job  market  is  expected  to  (103)_______ . However, to succeed  in  this  field,  one  must  stay  curious, adaptable, and (104)________. In the future, reaching for the stars might not be a dream, but a (105)_________.

Ravi  and  Arjun  had  been  rivals  on  the  football  field since their first year  in  school.  Both  were  talented  players,  and  their competition  often  brought  out  the  best-and  sometimes  the worst-in  them.  When  the  school  team  was  selected  for  the district  championship,  both  were  chosen  to  play.  At  first,  their rivalry  made  teamwork  difficult.  Passes  were  missed,  tempers (106)______ and the coach had to step in. He reminded them that personal pride should never come before the team. Slowly, Ravi and  Arjun began to (107)______ one another's strengths instead of focusing on their differences. As trust grew, their coordination improved,  and the team's performance soared. In the semi-final match,  it  was  a  pass  from  Ravi  that  helped  Arjun  score  the winning goal. The crowd cheered not just for the win, but for the sportsmanship.  What  began  as  a  clash  ended  in  a  strong (108)______ that taught them the value of unity, mutual (109)______ and shared (110)______.
SSC Stenographer 08/08/2025 (Shift 1)
